title: Two actual common tests realize successive boundary weights
statement: Let $N\hookrightarrow Z$ be a smooth closed pair of finite-type $\mathbf Q$-schemes and let $E$ be a finite ordered simple normal crossings boundary [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary] transverse to $N$ (its local equations restrict to distinct coordinate parameters on $N$). Let $I\subset\mathcal O_N$ be coherent and $d\ge1$. Write $\operatorname{ord}_x I=\sup\{q\ge0:I_x\subseteq\mathfrak m_x^q\}$, with value $\infty$ for zero, and $\operatorname{cosupp}(I,d)=\{x:\operatorname{ord}_xI\ge d\}$. A test transformation is an open restriction, a smooth-center blowup in cosupport with normal crossings with $E$, a product with a line adjoining its zero section to $E$, or a blowup of the intersection of two boundary hypersurfaces. For a cosupport blowup use the strict transform of $N$ and the ideal $e^{-d}\sigma^*I$, where $e$ is the exceptional equation; for the last two operations use ordinary pullback. Two such data on the same ambient scheme and with the same ordered boundary are test equivalent if their finite test sequences coincide. Let $(N,I,d)$ and $(P,J,b)$ be test equivalent, where $P$ is also smooth and has the same local dimension as $N$.  After any common finite sequence [def-trf-common-marked-test-sequence], write $(T,M_T,P_T)$ for its endpoints, $d_T,b_T$ for their marks, and take arbitrary support points $x\in M_T$, $y\in P_T$ with the same ambient image in both cosupports. For each current boundary label $H$, either both boundary orders are infinite, both are zero, or there are natural numbers $a,c,h,l,k$ with boundary orders $a,c$ and the following witnesses. For each $r\in\{0,1\}$ there is a common finite test sequence from the original pair to a pair $(U_r,A_r,B_r)$, with marks $d_T,b_T$, and two support points with the same ambient image in both cosupports. Their point orders are respectively $(k+r+1)a+h$ and $(k+r+1)c+l$. These are actual common sequences and point orders, not assumed normalized equalities.

proof.text: A missing boundary component has order zero on both supports. At a point on the component, zero completed ideals give infinite boundary orders. The proved point-order recovery and positivity of marks show that one completed ideal is zero iff the other is zero: nonzero formal ideals have finite point order.

proof.text: In the remaining nonzero case, the normal-slice and anisotropic calculation identify finite boundary orders a,c and residual orders h,l. Adjoin a line and iterate the exceptional-intersection blowup in its t chart. The substitution is u_1 -> t^k u_1 with ordinary pullback and unchanged marks. Coordinate charts and regularity over the perfect base field give smooth supports and transverse labelled boundaries. Total order never decreases, so the chosen points remain in cosupport.

proof.text: Choose k at least the two residual orders h,l. The anisotropic formula gives exact finite point orders (k+1)a+h and (k+1)c+l. Take the same construction with k+1 for the second witness, and concatenate both finite test words with the given common prefix. This produces the quantified geometric sequences, marks, points and order formulas.

lean.statement: theorem boundary_order_test_witnesses (S : Embedded (ULift.{u} ℚ)) (M P : Marked S) [LocallyOfFiniteType S.p] [QuasiCompact S.p] (hboundary : IsStrictNormalCrossingsBoundary (⨅ i : Fin S.boundary.length, S.boundary.get i)) (hordered : HasAdaptedNormalCrossingsCenter (⊥ : S.Z.IdealSheafData) (fun i ↦ S.boundary.get i)) (hM : HasAdaptedNormalCrossingsCenter (⊥ : M.N.IdealSheafData) (fun i ↦ (S.boundary.get i).comap M.j)) (hP : HasAdaptedNormalCrossingsCenter (⊥ : P.N.IdealSheafData) (fun i ↦ (S.boundary.get i).comap P.j)) (hdim : ∀ (x : M.N) (y : P.N), M.j x = P.j y → ringKrullDim (M.N.presheaf.stalk x) = ringKrullDim (P.N.presheaf.stalk y)) (hequivalent : RestrictedEquivalent M P) : ∀ (T : Embedded (ULift.{u} ℚ)) (M' P' : Marked T), CommonTestSequence M P M' P' → ∀ (x : M'.N) (y : P'.N), M'.j x = P'.j y → M'.j x ∈ M'.cosupport → P'.j y ∈ P'.cosupport → ∀ i : Fin T.boundary.length, (boundaryOrder M'.ideal ((T.boundary.get i).comap M'.j) x = ⊤ ∧ boundaryOrder P'.ideal ((T.boundary.get i).comap P'.j) y = ⊤) ∨ (boundaryOrder M'.ideal ((T.boundary.get i).comap M'.j) x = 0 ∧ boundaryOrder P'.ideal ((T.boundary.get i).comap P'.j) y = 0) ∨ ∃ a c h l k : ℕ, boundaryOrder M'.ideal ((T.boundary.get i).comap M'.j) x = (a : ℕ∞) ∧ boundaryOrder P'.ideal ((T.boundary.get i).comap P'.j) y = (c : ℕ∞) ∧ ∀ r : Fin 2, ∃ (U : Embedded (ULift.{u} ℚ)) (A B : Marked U), CommonTestSequence M P A B ∧ A.marking = M'.marking ∧ B.marking = P'.marking ∧ ∃ (z : A.N) (w : B.N), A.j z = B.j w ∧ A.j z ∈ A.cosupport ∧ B.j w ∈ B.cosupport ∧ order A.ideal z = (((k + r.val + 1) * a + h : ℕ) : ℕ∞) ∧ order B.ideal w = (((k + r.val + 1) * c + l : ℕ) : ℕ∞)
